summary: Pilocarpine is a muscarinic cholinergic agonist that stimulates exocrine gland secretion, increasing saliva and sweat. Oral tablets are used to relieve dry mouth (xerostomia) caused by head and neck radiotherapy or by Sjogren syndrome. Sweating is the most common adverse effect, and it must be used cautiously in asthma, cardiovascular disease, and narrow-angle glaucoma because of its parasympathomimetic actions.
indications: Treatment of symptoms of dry mouth from salivary gland hypofunction caused by radiotherapy for cancer of the head and neck
Treatment of symptoms of dry mouth in patients with Sjogren syndrome

dosage.d: 5 mg three times daily; may titrate to 10 mg three times daily
dosage.n: Allow 4-8 weeks to assess effect; max 30 mg/day
Taken with meals and at bedtime

dosage.n: Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment

admin: May be taken with or without food (food may delay onset)
Maintain adequate fluid intake to offset fluid loss from sweating
Allow several weeks of continuous therapy before judging effect
moa: Pilocarpine is a parasympathomimetic agonist that acts predominantly on muscarinic (M3) receptors of exocrine glands and smooth muscle. Stimulation of salivary and sweat gland muscarinic receptors increases secretion, relieving xerostomia. It also stimulates smooth muscle of the gastrointestinal and urinary tracts and can cause miosis and increased bronchial secretions.

absolute: Conditions where miosis is undesirable (acute iritis, narrow-angle/angle-closure glaucoma)
relative: Controlled asthma or COPD (risk of bronchospasm/secretions)
monitor: Hydration in patients with excessive sweating

preg: Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus; human data are limited.
lact: It is not known whether pilocarpine is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, a decision should be made to discontinue nursing or the drug.
renal: Limited data in renal impairment; use with caution and monitor for adverse effects.
hepatic: Mild impairment: no adjustment. Moderate impairment: start at 5 mg twice daily and titrate by response/tolerability. Severe hepatic impairment: use is not recommended.

interactions.food: Food slows the rate of absorption; a high-fat meal can reduce peak levels
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; limit alcohol as it can worsen dehydration

serious: Bronchospasm in patients with airway disease

monitoring: Degree of sweating and fluid/electrolyte status
Cardiovascular status (pulse, blood pressure) in at-risk patients
Respiratory symptoms in patients with reactive airway disease
Visual disturbance, especially with night driving
counsel: Drink extra fluids if you sweat a lot to avoid dehydration

pearls: Sweating is the most frequent dose-limiting adverse effect
Avoid in uncontrolled asthma and narrow-angle glaucoma due to muscarinic effects
Allow 4-8 weeks of therapy before deciding it is ineffective for xerostomia
Patients with significant cardiopulmonary disease need close monitoring
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose produces an exaggerated cholinergic syndrome: profuse sweating and salivation, lacrimation, bradycardia, hypotension, bronchospasm, nausea/vomiting, diarrhea, visual disturbance, and tremor. Management is supportive; atropine is the antidote for severe muscarinic effects, with supportive care for cardiovascular and respiratory function.
